mentor_notes: This setup teaches the 'post-breakout bull flag entry' pattern — one of the highest-probability swing setups in trending stocks. HDFCBANK completed a powerful surge from 738.65 (08-Jun) to 806.1 (30-Jun), then entered a controlled 6-session consolidation between 793-807, forming a tight range with progressively higher intraday lows. The visual cues to verify: (1) The flag's lower boundary (793-794) held across four consecutive sessions — each dip was bought, showing accumulation. (2) Volume dried up during the flag (~25-26M/day vs 41-45M during the surge) — classic 'flag on low volume' confirming distribution is absent. (3) Today's close at 801.50 in the upper third of the day's range shows intraday buyers remain in control. The key teaching: entries in the upper portion of a tight consolidation zone (near 800-803) after a strong momentum surge offer asymmetric risk — if the flag fails, the stop is defined at the base (793); if it resolves upward, the measured move target is the flag pole length (~67 pts) added to the breakout (~807), implying a mechanical target of ~874 in the longer swing, though our conservative T2 of 816 captures only the immediate structural resistance. The PCR < 0.7 warning is critical education: heavy call buying relative to puts often signals crowded bullish positioning that must be digested before price moves higher — this is why the setup is WATCH and not TRADE_READY.
